steps.content: The main lights in the interrogation room are off. Still, you sense that the person you're about to interrogate is at home.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Well, I'll be damned! Our beloved MBCC Chief is a young Adonis! You have a bright future ahead of you.
steps.female_content: Well, I'll be damned! Our beloved MBCC Chief is a young Aphrodite! You have a bright future ahead of you.

steps.content: McQueen delivers the compliment with a hint of sarcasm, which is hard to miss in the smile she gives you.
McQueen is a habitual liar. She can't be trusted. Lisa warned you the moment she learned about McQueen's arrival in the MBCC.
Nice to meet you, Miss McQueen.
Or should I call you Miss Art Dealer, Miss Forgery Trader, or Miss Former Painter?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Ah, looks like Lisa told you a lot about me. What else did she tell you?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Did she mention how incredibly stunning I am, or how unbelievably charismatic?
test
test
test
test
test
test
She said you are greasy, cunning, have no respect for other people's personal space, and are overly affectionate toward whoever you meet for the first time.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Yeah, that sounds like Miss Lisa.
It's also mentioned in the testimony that you may have a murky past, and that you detest the sickening Eastside ways.
McQueen neither confirms nor denies the claim. She just shrugs nonchalantly.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: She knows a lot, and talks a lot too.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: The intelligence was true; you are a crafty character, Chief. Even that reclusive, mean critic is willing to serve you.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: One thing the Eastside black market has in abundance is secret information. Word on the street is that you're a competent chief.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: So, are you interested in working with the McQueen Art Agency? I could use your talents. Together, we will make it big.
Bigger than making a replica of every single work of art on exhibition except Sosia, and distributing them around the market, all done in one night?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Lisa told you that?
No, she just suspected you may have had an ulterior motive for attending the exhibition. She doesn't make unsubstantiated claims. It's the MBCC that found out about what you did.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
You know the black market inside out, you're an expert in intelligence gathering, and you're an old hand at selling forgeries.
You create a forgery using your power, let it change hands a few times, so no one knows who the original owner is, then you appear among the rich as an art dealer to introduce the artwork to them.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Hahaha...

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Clever, huh? I've done this act over and over for so many years, and no one has been any the wiser.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Those businessmen in Eastside are self-proclaimed art lovers. They live lives of tremendous wealth and unfair privilege. But deep down, they are just a bunch of suckers, lost in the maze of lies and deception I create for them.

options: You do not deny your crimes?
Do you really have nothing to say to defend yourself?

choices.text: You do not deny your crimes?
Do you really have nothing to say to defend yourself?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Heh... I am confessing, dear.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Don't you already have hard evidence against me?
McQueen's finger traces the edge of the evidence bag, making its slow way toward your hand. All the while she is gazing at you, with a mischievous light in her eyes.

options: Be serious. This is the interrogation room.

choices.text: Be serious. This is the interrogation room.

steps.content: When did you start creating and selling forgeries? What's your purpose? Money?
What's this murky past of yours? Does it have anything to do with your business?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Easy, easy, hold your horses... You really don't know how to treat a lady, do you?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: So many questions... Which one should I start with?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Ha! I got it!
She makes a show of having a eureka moment, but remains inappropriately close to you.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Chief, do you want to hear a story? A long, long story...
A story? About your past?
She makes no response, but gives you a meaningful look.

options: Listen to what she has to say

choices.text: Listen to what she has to say

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: That's more like it. You'll find your answers in this story.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Once upon a time, there was an unknown painter named Jennie who entered Eastside's art world.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: The collectors recognized her skills as a painter, but thought she got nothing else going for her...

steps.speaker: Collector A
steps.content: A hardworking painter. Unfortunately, diligence is not a good selling point.

steps.speaker: Collector B
steps.content: Jennie? Never heard of her. Nice painting though. You can't be a successful artist without knowing how to publicize your works. This one didn't even bother to take out an ad.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Artistic expression... Dreams... No one in Eastside cares about these.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: But... not without exception.

steps.speaker: Woman in exhibition
steps.content: You painted this?

steps.speaker: Woman in exhibition
steps.content: I can see that you've got good skills. I like the clashing colors of your painting; a break with tradition. You are quite an original painter.

steps.speaker: Woman in exhibition
steps.content: But I've got this feeling that something is missing. Do you feel the same way? Such a shame.
The woman stands silently in front of the painting for a long time.
Jennie is on pins and needles, but refrains from saying anything.
It's some time before the woman turns around to face Jennie, smiling widely.

steps.speaker: Woman in exhibition
steps.content: Do you want to have your paintings exhibited in the Belphegor Art Museum? I can help you with that.

steps.speaker: Woman in exhibition
steps.content: You need this opportunity, I believe. And I don't want to miss a future star in the oil painting scene of DisCity.

steps.speaker: Woman in exhibition
steps.content: Here is my address. Call on me anytime.

steps.speaker: Woman in exhibition
steps.content: Ask for McQueen.
McQueen?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: It's just a name. Not me, the McQueen in the story.
Trust, attachment, longing, confusion, hatred... You don't know what feeling or feelings the name McQueen evokes in her.
Did Jennie visit McQueen?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: She did. Jennie saw McQueen as a mentor, a confidant.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: She shared everything about herself with McQueen. She told her about her feelings, about her dream... she told her everything.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: But to McQueen, Jennie was nothing more than a plaything.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: McQueen puts Jennie on a pedestal, but that's just her way of manipulating Jennie. She took advantage of Jennie's trust and reliance to coax her into painting for her. Did Lisa tell you about the painting?
McQueen raises her head, looking at you squarely in the eye.
Judy on the Blue Couch. You were Jennie. You created the forgery.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Not just this one, mind you. McQueen kept coming up with new excuses to cajole Jennie into painting more. And she always said it'd be the last time. Heh...

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Forget about the Belphegor Art Museum! Nothing's more important than tricking young people and turning them into meal tickets.
McQueen is being candid with you. She reveals her old name and miserable past, but she does so in such an offhand manner that you get the impression that she's recounting the story of someone else.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: As for Jennie, she awakened her power and became a Sinner. Then she did something juvenile. She wanted to vent her anger by revenging herself, so she took care of the evil art dealer with a knife. Good for her, huh?
You... Jennie killed McQueen and used her identity?
The seemingly genuine smile on her face baffles you.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Jennie... No more Jennie. Her story has ended; forget about her. She's a thing of the past.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: McQueen, on the other hand, is a microcosm of Eastside's art world. She is everything it stands for...

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: She is a representative of the Eastsiders.
Like an actor on stage at the end of a play, McQueen, still seated, mimes taking off a hat and bowing. She looks completely at ease in the interrogation room, but something feels off.
If she has really let go of her past, then what explained the appearance of the phantom of fear in the basement of the art museum?

options: You really have become the new McQueen?
But Jennie is not entirely gone.

choices.text: You really have become the new McQueen?
But Jennie is not entirely gone.

steps.content: You haven't put the past behind you. The frightening memories of creating and selling forgeries came back to you in the art museum, and you even...
You make no secret of your loathing and disgust when talking about the Eastside ways.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: So? You think I'm good at heart, Chief? And you want to convert me?
...You detest Eastside's art world, which doesn't value artistic expression. Then why are you using McQueen's name and doing what she used to do?
Stop copying the works that other people have put their hearts and soul into. Paint for yourself again; you still have the chance.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Paint for myself? Hahaha...
The sudden roar of laughter in the closed room grates on you.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: The MBCC didn't find out everything about me after all. You have no idea what else I've done, do you?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Ah, I shouldn't have been surprised that you didn't find out this other thing I'm doing, considering that they come to me of their own accord.
What? You're not just creating and selling forgeries?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: I've inherited McQueen's name and career. It's only natural for me to do everything she ever did and take it a step further.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Need I remind you that art dealers not only deal with potential buyers, but also painters?
You trick other artists into creating forgeries for you?
Selling forgeries to collectors who failed you to get back at them... isn't that enough?
You can make replicas easily with your power. Why are you dragging other artists into your business?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Why do you think I am doing that? I just don't understand why some artists are still holding on.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Dreams are nothing but an illusion, a lie they tell themselves that they can change this circle.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: All I'm doing is rewarding them for their efforts before their worlds are shattered by reality.
That's ridiculous!

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: You feel this way only because you've never been in that situation!
There is an unusual sparkle of excitement in her eyes.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Recognition, acclaim, money, fame... these were things that Jennie couldn't resist. Do you think today's painters can?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: I don't even need a McQueen to lure them into my game. I snap my fingers, and one Jennie after another comes rushing to me.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: It's a win-win situation all around. Hahaha!
She is in stitches, one hand on her belly.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Dear, one trip to the Belphegor Art Museum doesn't make you an expert on the art world.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: From top to bottom, from painter to buyer, the profession is rotten to the core.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Changes are out of the question. Since a paintbrush can't be washed clean in dirty water, we...

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Might as well make the water dirtier, and murkier!

options: The art world is not as corrupt as you make it out to be.

choices.text: The art world is not as corrupt as you make it out to be.

steps.content: There must be people out there who are pursuing their dreams. But what happened to you makes you so vindictive that you want to drag everyone down.
That won't change anything. It won't help you conquer your fear.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Change...
McQueen hasn't entirely recovered from the bout of excitement. She leans back in her chair, somewhat tired-looking, and looks at you coldly.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: I like the way you said the word change, so calm and naive.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: You fantasize about seeing it changed... Come and see if it can be changed.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Extravagant parties; repulsive, foolish tastes in art; moments of young artists being corrupted... It has everything.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Come and see the show. And you'll understand my point.
McQueen produces an invitation and inserts it between your fingers.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Those people... they aren't worth changing.

It was a successful interrogation.
McQueen admitted to all the accusations, revealed her old name and unsavory past, and even came clean about the other preposterous thing she's doing.

But the emotional distance between you and McQueen has not been shortened.
Her passiveness and madness are still beyond your comprehension.
Before stepping out of the interrogation room, she turns around abruptly and raises her right hand toward the harsh light overhead.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Just so you know, you can never take off the dark gloves once you've put them on.
